novelty_flags.one_line: Add Buchholz et al. (2023), “Learning Linear Causal Representations from Interventions under General Nonlinear Mixing”: it is a closer same-design comparator (unknown single-node targets and arbitrary nonlinear mixing) than several cited papers, though its latent SCM is linear Gaussian.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 3: simultaneous confidence edges
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The learned-ratio MMD guarantee assumes rather than derives the simultaneous evaluation-law L1 ratio-error event and uses a fixed, non-data-driven radius.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Familywise ancestral-edge validity conditional on the stated first-stage event, with unconditional coverage only after its declared 1-eta probability is combined.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Open-ended Question 1: generated-rank frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The target rate and expansion are conditional on a uniform C1(K) first-stage log-ratio contract; construction of a ratio learner attaining that contract is not claimed.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: A conditional second-stage generated-rank rate and expansion over Theta^beta_{G,s}(c,M,K,rho), given the stated first-stage contract and any additional asymptotically-linear first-stage representation.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3.2 gives bivariate identification from one perfect intervention per node under the continuous-witness condition (3.2); Theorem 3.4 uses a pair of perfect interventions per node for arbitrary dimension; Section 7 explicitly conjectures the one-per-node n>2 extension.

CauCA fixes G and intervention targets in its known-target model class; with one perfect stochastic intervention per node satisfying discrepancy, Theorem 4.2(ii) identifies up to elementwise diffeomorphisms.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 23-24, Assumption D.1 and Corollary D.1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Corollary D.1 obtains elementwise-diffeomorphic identification from one imperfect intervention per node under the supplied topological ordering of intervention targets; the paper says full-graph recovery requires further assumptions.
Theorem 3.4 identifies a maximal measurement model under a complete intervention family and no-imaginary-subset condition, up to isolated latent edges.
The article defines MMD as an RKHS integral-probability metric and supplies distribution-free two-sample concentration tests for observed samples; it does not analyze fitted likelihood-ratio inputs.

source_verification_receipts.version: Statistics and Probability Letters 201 (2023), 109886; theorem text corroborated by author preprint arXiv:2112.08546
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work gives uniform local-linear conditional-CDF bias, rate, and asymptotic-linear results for observed response thresholds and covariates; the publisher record confirms the cited 2023 article.

The paper studies nonparametric regression with nonparametrically generated covariates and derives a stochastic expansion, consistency rates, and asymptotic distributions; it does not address generated indicator thresholds in conditional-CDF estimation.
